_about: The Help Center's built-in setup guides (helpdesk.js adds each once; after that staff edit them on the site). Blocks: h, p, steps, img, video.

articles.title: Which apps does our church need?
articles.summary: Six apps, one team: who uses which, and what to buy first.

body.text: Central is six apps that find each other on your church's network. Each person uses the one that fits their job.

items: **Central Pedal** sits at the worship leader's or keys player's feet. Pads, multitracks with click and spoken cues, chord charts, lyrics, a looper and a guitar and keys rig. We build it and ship it ready to play.
**Central Pedal Control** is the pedal's app for your computer, tablet or phone. You build setlists, add songs and set up pads at home, then upload to the pedal.
**Central Control** runs on the desk computer (the main admin and admins). It runs lights, lyrics, slides, cameras, the stream, in-ears, the mix and the run sheet.
**Central Usage** is for each musician and singer: their chart, the lyrics, their instrument sound and their own in-ear mix.
**Central Services** is the schedule: who's serving, who's away and what's being played. Everyone in the church can have it.
**Central Production** is a free studio for making tracks, loops, pads, instruments and plugins.

body.text: Most churches start with a church pack (Lite, Regular, Plus or Ultra). A pack holds the Central Control, Central Usage and Central Pedal Control keys and the Central Services slots for your team. Add the pedal and the sound plans you want. Pricing → "Which plan do I need?" walks you through it.

articles.title: Setting up the Central Pedal
articles.summary: From the box to your first song: power, screens, sound, Wi-Fi and your first setlist.

body.text: Plug it in

items: Plug in the power supply that came with it. The pedal starts by itself; the 3.5" touch screen lights up after about 30 seconds.
For a big screen, plug a monitor into HDMI 1. HDMI 2 can show the lyrics to the room. Each port shows its own choice (Settings → Screens & touch).
Headphones or the desk go into the headphone jack (outputs 1–2). A DAC board, if yours has one, is outputs 3–4, and a USB audio interface comes after that.
Connect to the church Wi-Fi: Settings → Wi-Fi & devices. The other apps find the pedal on the same network.

body.alt: The Central Pedal's LIVE screen: the setlist on the left, the song's sections, PAUSE and NEXT in the middle, pads below

body.text: Check the sound

items: Settings → Sound → Test sound plays a tone on each output. You should hear outputs 1–2 in your headphones.
If you hear crackles but no music on the headphone jack, set Settings → Output device → Headphone jack buffer to Biggest.
Check where the sound goes shows which output each bus (tracks, pads, click and instrument) plays on.

body.text: Your first setlist

The easiest way is Central Pedal Control on your computer: + Add songs (your own MP3s or WAVs, a multitrack, or Central Tracks), arrange the setlist, then press Upload. On the pedal itself, open the Tracks tab to add songs from a USB stick.
Updates arrive by themselves: the pedal looks every few hours and installs in a quiet minute, never while something plays. Settings → Software updates shows what it's doing.

articles.title: The main admin's first hour
articles.summary: Make the church's account, install Central Control, give out keys and set up each computer's job.

items: On the website, Account → Make an account → "Set up a new church". Use the church's own email: that account owns the keys. Confirm the email we send.
Buy a church pack (Pricing). The keys appear under Account → My products and come by email.

Install Central Control on the desk computer (Downloads). On first start it asks for the church's name and a key, then for this computer's jobs: lyrics, lights, cameras, in-ears, tracks, the stream mix, slides.
Pick a 4-digit admin code when asked. It's needed later to change a computer's jobs.

Back on the website, Account → Your church & team: add your second main admin and your admins (Central Control), and your musicians and singers (Central Usage). Each gets an email with their key and download link.
Open Central Control's Devices tab: the pedal and every computer on the network show up there.

body.alt: Central Control's Devices tab, with the pedal and the church's computers

body.text: Up to 2 main admins per church. Main admins can change roles, people and billing; admins run the service.

articles.title: Adding admins, musicians and singers
articles.summary: Hand out keys from the Teams page, and take one back when someone moves on.

items: Sign in on the website as the church or a main admin and open Account → Your church & team.
Under Teams, add each person's name and email to Admins (Central Control), Users (Central Usage) or Pedal Control.
They get an email with their key, a link to download the app and how to sign in. Their key also shows under their own Account → My products.
To take a key back, press Remove next to the person. The key is free for the next person; their app asks for a key at its next check.
Musicians can also join with your church's code when they make their account. You'll find the code on the same page.

body.text: A Central Usage key works on two devices, so players can have one at church and one at home. A Central Control key is for one computer.

articles.title: For musicians and singers: Central Usage
articles.summary: Your chart, the lyrics, your sound and your own in-ear mix.

items: Open the email from your church and download Central Usage for your device. It runs on Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone, iPad and Android.
Sign in with the email your church used, or paste your key.
Pick your part (keys, guitar, bass, vocals…). The chart follows the song the pedal is playing, in the key and the clef you choose.
In-ears: plug headphones into your device or the interface you use, and set your own mix of the tracks and the band.
Instrument: plug in a keyboard or guitar and pick a sound. The sound plans add more.

body.alt: Central Usage's chord chart following the song

articles.title: Connecting Planning Center and CCLI
articles.summary: Bring your plans in, put the copyright line on screen and let the CCLI report fill itself in.

body.text: Planning Center

items: A main admin opens Account → Planning Center & CCLI on the website (or Central Control → Settings → Planning Center & CCLI) and presses Connect Planning Center.
Sign in to Planning Center and allow Motion Audio Central. Every device in your church then sees the upcoming plans.
Pick a plan to make a setlist. Songs are matched to Central Tracks and your own songs by CCLI number, then by title; anything missing is listed with how to get it.
Plans are checked for changes every 15 minutes, or press Check for changes.

body.text: Not connected yet? Import a plan from a file instead: a Planning Center CSV export, or a plain list of songs.
CCLI

items: Enter your CCLI licence number and streaming licence number on Account → Planning Center & CCLI.
Import songs from SongSelect (.txt or .usr files) or ChordPro in the song editor: words, chords, writers, copyright and the CCLI number come with them.
The copyright line shows on each song's first slide. You can move it to the last or every slide, or change its wording.
Each time a song's words reach a real screen it's counted, once per song a day. The CCLI report on your Account page downloads in the layout CCLI's reporting page asks for.

articles.title: Lights: first steps
articles.summary: Build your stage, add your real lights and make your first scene.

items: In Central Control, give one computer the Lights job (Settings → This computer's jobs), and connect it to your DMX interface or Art-Net node.
Lighting → Build my stage asks a few questions (stage size and shape, risers, screens, your room and seats, how many lights hang where) and builds the stage in 3D.
Add your real lights: Find a real light… searches 2,272 fixtures by maker and model. Pick the mode, the universe and the address. No match? Make a profile… lets you list the channels yourself.
Make a scene: + Scene starts from a preset look. Press Program lights to set colour, brightness, position, zoom, gobo and effects for any light, live.
Run it: pick a song and press Follow the show. The auto lights follow the sections; your scenes fire where you put them.
Simulate a setlist before Sunday: the 3D stage plays it without touching the real lights.

body.alt: The Lighting tab: the stage in 3D above the presets

articles.title: Slides, lyrics and the band's screen
articles.summary: Lyrics on a background, slides from the designer, scripture in seconds and a confidence monitor for the band.

items: Lyrics come from each song's lyrics and follow the track. Under Lyrics pick a background for every song, one song or one part of a song; it crossfades.
The confidence monitor shows the band the current lines in yellow and the next in white, with chords, a clock and time left. Settings → Confidence monitor on the lyrics computer changes all of it.
Slides: make decks in the designer (text, pictures, video, shapes, themes and transitions), or import pictures, PDFs and PowerPoint. Show mode puts Preview and Live side by side.
Scripture in seconds: type "John 3:16" or "Ps 23:1-4" and it becomes slides plus a lower third for the stream. King James, World English, American Standard and Reina-Valera 1909 are built in.
The video manager decides which screen shows what: lyrics, slides, a camera or the stream.

body.alt: Central Control's Slides tab with Preview and Live

articles.title: The stream and automatic shorts
articles.summary: Stream the service, record it, and let the built-in AI make short clips for social media.

items: Give a computer the Stream mix job. The Video tab sends the program to your stream destinations (RTMP or SRT) with its own mix.
Record the service with one button on the Mix tab, or set it to record by itself.
After a recording of 10 minutes or more, Shorts finds the songs and the sermon and makes vertical clips with captions and draft titles.
Review them on the Shorts tab of the main admin's computer: play, trim, fix captions, approve or delete.
Post to YouTube, Facebook, Instagram and TikTok once each is connected (Shorts → Settings), or download and post by hand.

body.text: How many shorts, how long, and the sermon and worship mix are all in Shorts → Settings.

articles.title: Central Production basics
articles.summary: Make a track, a pad, an instrument or a plugin, and use it in your other apps.

items: Open Central Production (the app, or /production/ on this website) and sign in to save projects to your account.
File → New project asks what you're making: a track, loop, sample, pad, instrument, plugin or pedal board. The project opens set up for that.
Settings → Audio picks your interface, which input each track records from, and measures the delay so recordings line up.
Record with count-in, punch in and out, or loop takes. The mixer has sends, buses and automation; the piano roll has quantize and humanize.
Export WAV, MP3 or stems. Install into my apps puts what you made into Central Control and Central Usage on this computer. Publish sends it to Make & sell or Central Tracks.

body.text: Central Production is free. The sound plans unlock the better sounds inside it.

articles.title: Delays that stay in time with the song
articles.summary: Every delay can follow the song's tempo on a note you pick, or keep its own time.

body.text: Every delay in the apps has a Sync to tempo switch. Turn it on and pick a note (a quarter, a dotted eighth, an eighth triplet and so on). The repeats then land on that note at the song's tempo, and they move with it when the next song is faster or slower. Turn it off and the delay keeps the time you set in milliseconds.

items: Pedal boards (the Central Pedal, Central Control and Central Usage): select a delay pedal, turn on Sync to tempo and pick the note. The pedal's time knob follows the song's tempo from then on.
Tracks, pads and the buses (the Central Pedal): open FX, then under Delay pick the note. With Central Plugins you can turn Sync to tempo off and set the time in milliseconds instead.
Central Control's shared delay (Mix → Reverb & delay): pick a note, or Free (ms). Channel inserts that are delays have their own Sync to tempo.
Central Production and the Central Usage Studio: the Delay effect has Sync to tempo, a note and a time. It follows tempo changes in the song, and exports keep them.
Central FX delays (Delay, Tape Echo, Ping-Pong) have Sync to tempo with a note. The Dotted Eighth Delay follows the tempo by itself; switch Sync to song tempo off to set its tempo by hand.
Building your own plugin: select a Delay block and pick a note under Sync to tempo. The plugin gets a Tempo knob, and the apps turn it to the song's tempo.

body.text: Delays saved before version 10.4 keep the sound they had. A few third-party pedals (the multiband delays, Zyn Echo, mda Delay, the Tape Delay, Delayorama and TAP Echo) have no time knob the apps can set exactly, so set those by ear.

articles.title: Keys, devices and renewals
articles.summary: Where your keys are, moving a key to a new computer, and what renewing does.

items: Every key you or your church owns is on Account → My products, with the devices it's on and a Copy button. They're in your email too.
Moving to a new computer: press Release next to the old device, then enter the key on the new one.
Sound plans come as one package key that works on three of your devices at once, each a different app (for example Central Usage, Central Control and your pedal).
Central Control keys include ten releases of updates (buy during 10.x and you're covered up to 11.0). Renew for $20 any time; your apps keep working if you don't.
Sound plans and Central Tracks Unlimited renew every year or month. Cancel any time from Account → Billing.

articles.title: No sound? A checklist
articles.summary: Go through these in order: most problems are found in the first three.

items: On the pedal, Settings → Sound → Test sound. Hear the tone? Then it's the routing: Check where the sound goes shows each bus's output.
No tone either: Play on each sound card plays straight on each card. Silent too? It's the cable, the headphones or the socket.
Crackles but no music on the headphone jack: Settings → Output device → Headphone jack buffer → Biggest.
A USB interface: plug it in before you start, and check it shows under Settings → Output device. Its outputs come after the jack (and the DAC board).
Still nothing? Contact support from Help on this website or from Settings → About in any app; it sends us what we need to look.

articles.title: Update failed, "can't reach the website" or the pedal is offline
articles.summary: What each message means and what to do.

body.text: An update failed

The apps download updates from GitHub. On Linux, an update waits while the computer installs its own updates, then tries again; it tells you the real reason if it can't. Settings → Software updates has Try again, and you can always download the newest version from Downloads.
"Couldn't reach the Motion Audio website"

Check this device is online. The status page (/status) shows whether sign-in, downloads and payments are working right now. Your apps keep working offline; they check your key again when they're back online.
The pedal shows as offline

items: Check the pedal is on and on the same Wi-Fi as the computer (Settings → Wi-Fi & devices on the pedal).
Some church networks keep devices apart. Ask whoever runs the network to allow devices to see each other, or use a network cable.
In Central Control or Central Pedal Control, type the pedal's address (shown on its Settings → About) into Connect.
